subject: Exhibit B: packaging & fee-bucket simplification — proposed redline
messages:
From: Amelia Jenkins <amelia.jenkins@orchidhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@orchidlegal.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on Exhibit B mapping + caps/floors

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our finance team flagged two areas in Exhibit B that need clarity before we can sign: the packaging mapping between "Core" vs "Burst" buckets (the mapping table on p.4) and the interaction between the monthly cap and the annual floor true-up (section 3.2).

Specifically:
- The table has three SKU groups but our onboarding team expects four logical bundles; we need deterministic mapping so billing won't flip mid-quarter.
- The cap language is multiplicative with the floor in a way that could create a month where we owe a large true-up unexpectedly.

Can Redwood provide a redline that simplifies the mapping (preferably a two-bucket approach) and an alternative cap/floor phrasing that limits single-month downside? Rajiv is copied for legal review.

Also can you attach the most recent order schedule in spreadsheet form so we can run scenarios?

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if easier.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Jenkins
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Orchid Health

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Jenkins <amelia.jenkins@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B mapping + caps/floors

Amelia — thanks for laying this out. Attaching a concise redline (Orchid_ExhibitB_redline_v1.pdf) and an annotated OrderSchedule spreadsheet that maps current SKUs to the simplified buckets. Key changes in the redline (summary):

1) Packaging simplification
- Replace the three-row SKU matrix with two runtime buckets: "Steady" (baseline commit) and "Burst" (on-demand above commit). The spreadsheet highlights the SKU->bucket mapping per your onboarding taxonomy.
- Deterministic mapping rule: SKUs with sustained monthly usage > 60% of historical baseline are treated as Steady; otherwise Burst. This avoids mid-quarter flips unless usage pattern changes for 2 consecutive months (operational guardrail).

2) Cap / Floor rewording
- Substitute the current multiplicative language in §3.2 with a "monthly-effective-cap" construct: the monthly cap sets an upper token billing for that month; the annual floor remains subject to a single annual true-up calculated on aggregate usage to avoid single-month volatility.
- Add a 30-day notification and 60-day cure window before any true-up is invoiced (operational protection for you).

3) Implementation notes
- We'll keep the existing SLA credits and carveouts for scheduled maintenance.
- Suggested DocuSign flow: Exhibit B redline + OrderSchedule will be the only redlined attachments to the main order form; no change to Master Services Agreement.

Next steps: please have Rajiv and your finance team scan the redline + spreadsheet. If you agree in principle we can incorporate the single tweak Rishi may propose and then generate a final PDF for signature. If you prefer a short call, Karthik and I are available this afternoon (2–4pm PT).

Attachments: Orchid_ExhibitB_redline_v1.pdf, OrderSchedule_Orchid-ORC-2026-042.xlsx

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, East
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Amelia Jenkins <amelia.jenkins@orchidhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B mapping + caps/floors — legal comments

Team / Amelia — quick legal pass on Grace's proposal: overall looks good and much simpler. A few suggested tweaks to the redline (I'll add these as tracked comments in the attached PDF):

- §2.1 (definition of "Burst"): replace the usage threshold language with an objective math formula (e.g., 60% of trailing-3-month median) to avoid subjective disputes.
- §3.2 (monthly-effective-cap): include an explicit definition of "Cap Credits" — how credits reduce billed tokens for the month (preserve order-of-operations for stacking with promotional credits).
- True-up mechanics: limit Redwood's ability to accelerate invoicing for a true-up to instances where there is suspected fraud or clear data reconciliation errors — otherwise we must follow the 60-day cure and a 30-day invoice dispute period.

I've attached the current Exhibit B for reference (Orchid_ExhibitB_current.pdf). I'll upload a commented PDF with inline redline language before EOD. If Orchid legal prefers different math for the bucket threshold, we can accept a mutually-agreed formula but need to lock the measurement window and data sources (billing system snapshot date).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@orchidlegal.com>
To: Amelia Jenkins <amelia.jenkins@orchidhealth.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:58:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B mapping + caps/floors — Orchid legal redline

Grace / Rishi — thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed the redline and Orchid is comfortable with the two-bucket approach in principle. A couple of minor points from our side:

- Cap definition: we propose replacing the word "billed tokens" with "billed units" and adding a parenthetical that ties units to the OrderSchedule SKU mapping to avoid interpretation disputes across product changes.
- True-up remedy: we accept the annual aggregate true-up but request that any invoice resulting from the true-up be netted against the immediately following month's invoice rather than issued as a separate invoice (operational preference).

Those are minor and do not block progress. Please circulate a final redline incorporating Rishi's objective measurement formula (trailing-3-month median) and the small cap wording tweak and we'll sign once DocuSign is ready.

Regards,
Rajiv Singh
Partner, Orchid Legal Counsel
rajiv.singh@orchidlegal.com

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Jenkins <amelia.jenkins@orchidhealth.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@orchidlegal.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Exhibit B mapping + caps/floors — next steps

Team — great, thanks for the alignment. Action items from Redwood's side:

1) Rishi will incorporate the trailing-3-month median formula and the explicit "billed units (as mapped in OrderSchedule)" parenthetical into Orchid_ExhibitB_redline_v2.pdf (target: 11/23 EOD).
2) Karthik will regenerate the OrderSchedule spreadsheet with the SKU->bucket formula visible and include a scenario tab that shows the annual true-up netting as Rajiv requested.
3) I will prepare the DocuSign envelope that includes the Master Order Form (clean), Exhibit B (redline v2), and OrderSchedule (final). Expect the DocuSign link from me once Rishi confirms the PDF.

If Orchid wants an expedited signature path, we can do an internal Exec OK and limited signature path on your side; happy to sync on timing.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to closing this week.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, East
Redwood Inference
Attachments: (will attach ExhibitB_redline_v2 and OrderSchedule final in follow-up)
